rag.answer:
# DNA Damage Response and Aggressive/Treatment-Refractory Phenotypes

The corpus provides evidence linking DDR alterations to aggressive disease across multiple tumor types:

## Endometrial Cancer
CNV-high endometrioid tumors with DDR alterations show prognosis similar to aggressive serous histotypes (PMID:32059776). These tumors demonstrate elevated DNA damage signaling (high DDR scores) across multiple genomic subtypes (CNV-high, POLE, and MSI), suggesting active DDR engagement is associated with more aggressive biology regardless of molecular subtype.

## Prostate Cancer
In metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC), alterations in DDR pathway genes (BRCA1, BRCA2, ATM) are frequent and associated with treatment challenges. The high frequency of somatic events involving DNA repair proteins correlates with aggressive phenotypes, particularly in tumors with high proliferation rates reflecting replication stress (PMID:26928463).

## Pancreatic and Ovarian Cancer
Ovarian cancer shows genome integrity disruptions dominating both germline and somatic alterations, with 23 of 36 predisposition genes affecting genome integrity belonging to Core DDR genes (BRCA1, BRCA2, CHEK2, ATM) (PMID:29625049). Similar patterns appear in pancreatic adenocarcinoma.

## Cross-Cancer Pattern
However, the corpus also notes complexity: DDR alterations don't uniformly predict aggressive outcomes. In metastatic colorectal cancer, DDR pathway alterations don't reliably indicate homologous recombination deficiency or predict platinum sensitivity (PMID:32730818), suggesting DDR alterations' prognostic significance varies by cancer type.
